item.title: [7] Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
item.description:
Last authors: Ke He, Hao Zhang

Authors: Ruidong Li, Shuai Yang, Wenyu Song, et al.

Score 7/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Experimental study of Majorana zero modes in hybrid nanowires, a relevant topic in topological superconductivity.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #Majorana #experiment #topologicalsuperconductivity

Abstract: Superconductor–semiconductor coupling plays a crucial role in realizing Majorana zero modes in hybrid nanowire devices. Here, the authors demonstrate controllable and tunable coupling in PbTe–Pb hybrid nanowires. More importantly, they establish a direct connection between the coupling strength and the emergence of robust zero modes. These findings provide valuable insights into engineering Majorana zero modes in this promising material platform.

item.title: [7] Quantum Hall transformer in a quantum point contact over the full range of transmission
item.description:
Last authors: Stuart Yi-Thomas, Jay D. Sau

Score 7/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Connects sliding charge density waves to fractional quantum Hall states; broad user interest.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #topic #quantumHall #chargedensitywave

Abstract: A quantum point contact between fractional quantum Hall states with different fillings can act as a dissipationless voltage transformer and provide a physical realization of the boundary sine-Gordon model. However, the microscopic understanding across the full range of transmission has remained unclear, complicating the interpretation of a recent experiment. Here, the authors use analytical and tensor network calculations of a sliding charge density wave to solve this open problem and quantitatively connect the conductance to the boundary sine-Gordon model.

item.title: [8] Observation of gapped Dirac magnons in a Co bilayer grown on Ru(0001)
item.description:
Last authors: Arthur Ernst, Christopher Hins

Authors: Khalil Zakeri, Arthur Ernst, Christopher Hins

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental evidence for Dirac-like excitations in a magnetic 2D system.

Tags: #method #spectroscopy #magnon

Abstract: Long celebrated in graphene, Dirac physics inspires the search for similar phenomena in magnonic systems. Here, the authors experimentally demonstrate that magnons in an epitaxial Co bilayer on Ru(0001) exhibit Dirac properties near the Brillouin zone corner. Remarkably, the substrate does not destroy the essential physics; despite breaking sublattice symmetry and opening a gap, local valley topology remains intact. Beyond opening possibilities for discovering Dirac magnons in other ultrathin 3 d magnetic films, these findings hold promise for on-chip magnonic applications.

item.title: [7] Dynamical magnetism in the disordered cubic lattice material γ−Ba3CoNb2O9
item.description:
Last authors: A. T. M. Nazmul Islam, Bella Lake

Authors: Fanjun Xu, Ralf Feyerherm, Cecilie Glittum, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental neutron study of unconventional spin fluctuations in a disordered quantum magnet.

Tags: #experiment #Ba3CoNb2O9 #neutron-scattering

Abstract: Strong disorder normally favors spin-glass freezing. Here, in contrast, the authors report an unconventional, highly fluctuating spin state in cubic γ-Ba 3 CoNb 2 O 9 with effective spin-½ moments randomly diluted to just above the percolation limit. Neutron and muon measurements, with partially overlapping time windows, surprisingly reveal persistent correlated spin fluctuations from picoseconds to microseconds—a behavior reminiscent of quantum spin liquids. Numerical calculations suggest singlet formation is important. These results show disorder can sustain dynamic spin correlations even without strong geometrical frustration.

item.title: [8] Magnetic symmetry implications of the zero- and applied-field Hall effect of UNi4B
item.description:
Last authors: F. Ronning, E. D. Bauer

Authors: Z. W. Riedel, W. S. Simeth, S. M. Thomas, F. Ronning, E. D. Bauer

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental Hall effect study on noncollinear antiferromagnet UNi4B with anomalous Hall implications.

Tags: #experiment #UNi4B #anomalous-hall

Abstract: The authors report here two finite zero-field Hall resistivity tensor components associated with the debated magnetic ground state of the noncollinear antiferromagnet UNi 4 B. For a commensurate magnetic structure, the finite Hall resistivity components cannot be explained by the formation of magnetic domains but are compatible with a monoclinic magnetic symmetry lower than that of previously proposed magnetic ordering models. Additional field-dependent Hall resistivity data collected up to 16 T suggest a notable intrinsic contribution to the anomalous Hall effect.
